note: Real-data references bundled with the app. No live fetch happens at runtime. These are published magnitudes and variable lists, not individual astronaut records — individual astronaut health records are not open (Privacy Act / IRB).

sources.name: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) / GeneLab — kidney dysfunction in spaceflight
sources.use: Evidence base that kidney function changes in spaceflight. No stone-incidence rate is claimed — none is quoted.
sources.what: GeneLab-based publications on kidney dysfunction are listed among the OSDR paper's example discoveries.

sources.name: NASA Life Sciences Portal (NLSP) / HRP Standard Measures
sources.use: Defines the variables this app logs, so a flight surgeon recognises the schema.
sources.what: The exact set of physiological and psychological measurements NASA collects across crews: fluid intake, urine output, body mass, exercise dose.

sources.name: NASA Human Research Program — bone loss and calcium
sources.use: The mechanism linking bone to kidney stones — and the labelled proxy for the calcium-load driver in the score.
sources.what: Bone mineral density loss of 1–2% per month without countermeasures; released calcium enters blood and urine.

sources.name: Barger et al., Lancet Neurology 2014 — sleep in space
sources.use: Sleep < 6 h is a scoring driver; crew sleep baselines are calibrated to this range.
sources.what: Astronauts are scheduled 8.5 h of sleep but average 5.96 h (shuttle) / 6.09 h (ISS) per night.
